headline: Solar marketing agency in Noida: reaching homeowners, RWAs and factories
card_text: Noida's sector kothis, high-rise societies and industrial phases buy solar in very different ways. Here's who decides, which DISCOM they deal with and the channels that reach them.
intro:
If you're looking for a solar marketing agency in Noida, the first thing to know is that Noida isn't one market. The planned sectors near the city centre are full of independent houses with usable roofs. The Expressway and Noida Extension belt is mostly high-rise societies, where the buyer is an RWA committee. And the industrial phases hold thousands of factories and warehouses with big daytime power bills. Each group searches differently, decides differently and needs a different pitch.

This guide is for installers, EPCs and dealers selling rooftop solar in Noida and Greater Noida. It covers the local facts your ads have to get right, how to reach each buyer, and how to judge whether your marketing is working. It's the same approach we use with the 30+ solar EPCs and manufacturers we work with across India.

sections.h2: The three solar buyers in Noida
sections.html:
Start by deciding which of these groups you want, because one ad can't speak to all of them:

BuyerTypical areasWho decidesWhat they ask about
Independent house and kothi ownersOlder planned sectors such as 14–15A, 19–30, 36–41, 44, 50–51 and similar plotted pocketsThe owner, usually with familyMonthly savings, roof space, panel and inverter brands, subsidy
High-rise housing societiesNoida Expressway sectors, sectors 75–79 and 137, Noida Extension (Greater Noida West)RWA or AOA committee, then residentsCommon-area bills, roof waterproofing, who maintains the plant
Factories, warehouses and institutionsNoida Phase 1, 2 and 3 industrial sectors, Greater Noida industrial areas, schools and hospitalsOwner, plant head or finance teamPayback period, capex vs RESCO, downtime during installation

Flat owners in societies usually can't install solar on their own, so a lead form that attracts them wastes calls. Builder floors are a smaller group in Noida than in Delhi or Gurugram, but where they exist, roof rights need checking first.

sections.h2: Noida facts your ads and sales calls must get right
sections.html:
Noida buyers compare several quotes, and many will check what you say. Keep these local points accurate:

  • Two DISCOMs. Most of Noida city is served by Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (PVVNL), a state DISCOM. Greater Noida is largely served by Noida Power Company Limited (NPCL), a private company. Net-metering applications, meter changes and load enhancement go through whichever one is on the customer's bill, so ask for the bill before you explain the process.
  • Central subsidy. Under PM Surya Ghar, eligible residential consumers can get central financial assistance of up to ₹78,000 for a system of 3 kW or more. RWAs and group housing societies can get support for common facilities at a separate per-kW rate. Check pmsuryaghar.gov.in for the current amounts before every campaign.
  • UP state top-up. Uttar Pradesh has offered an extra state subsidy for residential rooftop systems, announced at ₹15,000 per kW up to ₹30,000. State schemes are revised and depend on budget, so confirm the current position with UPNEDA before putting any state figure in an ad.
  • Net-metering rules. Rooftop solar in UP follows the UPERC rooftop solar regulations, which have been amended several times. Say that net metering is available subject to DISCOM approval, and keep your explanation in line with the current regulation.
  • Sanctioned load. A residential system generally can't be larger than the connection's sanctioned load. Many Noida kothis need a load increase first, and your team should mention this on the first call.

Never call it "free solar" or promise a subsidy as certain. Our guide to PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads has wording that stays accurate when the scheme changes.

sections.h2: What a solar marketing agency in Noida should do differently
sections.html:
A Noida campaign that treats the whole city as one location pin will mix kothi owners, tenants and flat owners in the same lead list. Here's what we do instead as a solar marketing agency covering all of NCR:

  1. Build targeting from sectors. Noida is numbered, which makes it easy. List the sectors your install team can serve in a day, then set Meta and Google location targeting by pincode or radius around those sectors.
  2. Match the ad to the roof. Kothi ads show full rooftop systems and monthly bill savings. Society ads talk about common-area bills, lifts, pumps and DG costs. Factory ads talk about payback and daytime load.
  3. Say Noida and Greater Noida separately. People search "solar panel installation in Greater Noida" and "solar company in Noida Extension" as different places. Use the names your buyers use on your landing pages and Google Business Profile.
  4. Use local proof. A short video of an installation in a recognisable Noida sector does more than stock images. Only use sites where the customer has agreed.
  5. Plan for slow buyers. Societies and factories take weeks or months. They need retargeting, a proposal and follow-up, not just a lead form.

For the search side, our guide to Google Ads for solar companies covers keywords, negatives and bidding in more detail.

Noida and Noida Extension have some of the densest clusters of high-rise societies in NCR, so this is a big opportunity, but it's a committee sale. A few things make it easier:

  • Find the person who sees the bills. The RWA or AOA treasurer, secretary or facility manager usually knows the common-area electricity cost. Start there.
  • Size the proposal to their roof. Tower roofs often carry water tanks, lift rooms and other equipment, so free area is limited. Be honest about what can fit and what share of common-area load it can offset.
  • Answer the usual objections in writing. Waterproofing, structure load, who cleans the panels, warranty, and what happens if the RWA changes. A one-page summary the committee can forward helps a lot.
  • Check who handed over the society. Some societies are still with the builder or have an ad hoc committee. Know who can sign before you invest weeks in the pitch.

Paid ads play a support role here. Committee members will look you up, so your Google reviews, website and project videos need to be ready before you pitch. We cover a similar process in our guide to solar marketing in Gurgaon, where society sales follow a comparable pattern.

sections.h2: Commercial and industrial solar in Noida
sections.html:
The industrial phases and Greater Noida's industrial areas hold small and mid-sized manufacturers, garment units, electronics assemblers and warehouses. Many run mostly in daytime, which suits solar well. Marketing to them works differently from home solar:

  • Lead with payback and monthly savings, stated as an estimate based on their bills.
  • Offer both capex and RESCO or OPEX options if you can deliver them, and explain the difference simply.
  • Ask for the last 12 months of bills and the sanctioned load before you quote.
  • Expect three or four conversations: the owner, the plant head, the finance person and sometimes the landlord if the shed is rented.

Google Search, LinkedIn and direct outreach usually do better here than broad Meta campaigns, because the audience is small and specific.

Filter every Noida lead before you send a surveyor:

  1. Do you own the property? Is it an independent house, builder floor, society or commercial unit?
  2. Which sector is it in, and is your bill from PVVNL or NPCL?
  3. What is your average monthly bill and sanctioned load?
  4. When do you want to install?

Then track each lead from source to installation: called, site visit booked, quote sent, installed. Each week, look at cost per qualified enquiry, cost per site visit, time to first call and quote-to-install rate by sector.

For reference, our rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when they're working well, and solar clients at scale typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week. Your results will depend on your sectors, offer and follow-up, and no agency can promise them in advance. We start with a 90-day sprint and then move to a flexible arrangement. You can see the kind of work involved in our solar portfolio: the Solarxp website, Sungrid's Google reviews and local SEO, Skynxt Solar's video and social, and RK Solar's lead generation.

faqs: Which is the best solar marketing agency in Noida?

Look for an agency that works only or mainly with solar businesses, can show solar case studies and measures cost per site visit, not just cost per lead. Performance and Pixel focuses on solar marketing and serves installers across Delhi NCR, including Noida and Greater Noida, from our office in Dwarka.
Which DISCOM handles solar net metering in Noida?

Most of Noida city is served by PVVNL, while Greater Noida is largely served by NPCL. The application goes to whichever DISCOM issues the customer's bill, so check the bill and the DISCOM's current process before explaining it.
Is there a state solar subsidy in Noida on top of PM Surya Ghar?

Uttar Pradesh has offered a state top-up for residential rooftop solar on top of the central PM Surya Ghar assistance. Amounts and availability can change, so confirm the current scheme with UPNEDA before using it in ads or quotes.
Can a flat owner in a Noida society install rooftop solar?

Usually not individually, because the roof is common property. Solar for societies is normally installed by the RWA or AOA for common areas, so installers should pitch the committee rather than individual flat owners.
How much does solar marketing cost in Noida?

It depends on your ad budget and the agency's fee. Our rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when working well, but your cost will depend on the sectors you target, your offer and how fast your team follows up.
